skill.name: wcag-validator
skill.description: Automatically validate Moodle templates, JavaScript, and CSS for WCAG 2.1 Level AA accessibility compliance. Checks semantic HTML, ARIA patterns, keyboard navigation, color contrast, and screen reader compatibility. Activates when working with Mustache templates, AMD modules, or discussing accessibility, a11y, WCAG, screen readers, or keyboard navigation.

generated_query: I'm building a new Moodle activity plugin and need help making sure my user interface is accessible. I have a Mustache template for a form that collects user feedback, with fields for name, email, rating (radio buttons), and a comment textarea. There's also a JavaScript AMD module that shows a live preview of the rating as the user selects options. Could you review my template and JS code for WCAG 2.1 Level AA compliance? I'm particularly worried about proper label associations, error handling for required fields, keyboard navigation between the radio buttons, and ensuring the live preview updates are announced to screen readers. I can share the code if you need it.

edit_instructions.rationale: Deleting the Screen Reader Announcements section removes all guidance on implementing live region updates in JavaScript, which is exactly what the user needs for their AMD module's rating preview.
